title: Open Calculator
body:
Open index.html.
Select Start 128K.
Click the display to focus it.

Choose Calculator
in the Spectrum menu.
tip:
This guide uses a PC keyboard.
Mouse clicks are highlighted.
speech: Open index dot H T M L in your browser, select Start 128 K, then click the display to connect your keyboard.
In the Spectrum menu, press Down twice to highlight Calculator, then press Enter.

title: Find your way
body:
Click a cell to select it.
Arrows move the selection.
Tab moves right.

Cyan headers show
your current row and column.
tip:
Use Edit, Clear, Copy,
Help, and Exit in the toolbar.
speech: Each box is a cell. Click a cell, or use the arrow keys, to select it. The cyan headers show your current row and column.
The F X bar shows the selected cell's contents. The toolbar provides Edit, Clear, Copy, Help, and Exit.

title: Type some labels
body:
A1: ITEM
B1: QTY
C1: PRICE
D1: TOTAL

Typing starts a new entry.
Enter saves it and moves down.
tip:
The yellow FX bar means
you are editing a cell.
speech: Let's build a small shopping list. Enter Item in A one, Quantity in B one, Price in C one, and Total in D one. We use Q T Y as a short label for Quantity.
Typing starts a new entry. Press Enter to confirm it and move down one row.

title: Enter the values
body:
A2: PENS
B2: 3        C2: 2.50

A3: NOTEBOOKS
B3: 2        C3: 4.75

Decimals accept . or ,
tip:
Click the cell you want,
then type and press Enter.
speech: For the first item, enter Pens in A two, a quantity of three in B two, and a price of two point five zero in C two.
On row three, enter Notebooks, a quantity of two, and a price of four point seven five.
You can use either a decimal point or a decimal comma.

title: Calculate a total
body:
Select D2 and type:

=B2*C2

Press Enter.
The result is 7.5.
tip:
Every formula starts with =
* means multiplication.
speech: Select D two and type equals B two times C two. Use the asterisk for multiplication, then press Enter.
The result is seven point five. Select D two again to see the saved formula in the F X bar. Every formula begins with an equals sign.

title: Copy a formula
body:
Select D2.
Drag its small bottom-right
square down to D3.

The references adjust
to the new row.
tip:
Copying replaces the
destination cell's contents.
speech: Select D two. Drag the small square at its bottom-right corner down to D three, and release the mouse.
The copied formula becomes B three times C three, giving nine point five. Relative references adjust automatically. Copying replaces any existing destination contents.

title: Add a grand total
body:
Put TOTAL in C4.
In D4, enter:

=SUM(D2:D3)

The grand total is 17.
tip:
Keep the SUM cell outside
the range it adds together.
speech: Put the label Total in C four. In D four, enter equals SUM, open parenthesis, D two, colon, D three, close parenthesis.
This adds both line totals and gives seventeen. Put the sum outside its own range to avoid a circular reference.

title: Edit or cancel
body:
Select B2, then click FX
or choose Edit.

Save / Enter = confirm
Cancel / Escape = discard

Change the quantity 3 to 4.
tip:
Backspace removes a character.
Existing formulas recalculate.
speech: To edit existing contents, select a cell and click the F X bar, or choose Edit. Backspace removes a character.
The yellow bar shows your pending entry. Cancel, or Escape, discards the edit. We first cancel a trial change, keeping the original value.
Now change B two from three to four and choose Save. The formulas recalculate, and the grand total becomes nineteen point five.

title: Clear a cell
body:
Select the cell first.
Click Clear, or press Delete.

Here we remove a
temporary note in A6.
tip:
Check the selected address
before clearing a cell.
speech: To erase a cell, select it and click Clear, or press Delete. Here we add and then clear a temporary note in A six.
Our shopping list and its formulas stay in place. Always check the selected cell address before clearing.

title: Explore the sheet
body:
The sheet has columns A-H
and 64 rows.

[<] [>] switch column pages.
UP moves up 16 rows.
DOWN moves down 16 rows.
code:
4 columns x 16 rows
visible at a time
tip:
The range indicator tells you
which rows are on screen.
speech: The sheet has eight columns, A through H, and sixty-four rows. Four columns and sixteen rows are visible at a time.
Use the controls below the grid to switch column pages or jump sixteen rows. The up and down buttons move by sixteen rows. Your data remains as you navigate.

title: Keyboard copy
body:
Select a source cell.
Press F5 to begin copying.
Use arrows to choose the end.
Enter applies; Escape cancels.

Copy also accepts a destination
click, then Apply.
tip:
Relative references move.
$A$1 stays fixed when copied.
speech: For keyboard copying, select the source cell and press F five. Use the arrows to choose the destination corner. Enter applies the copy, and Escape cancels it.
We first cancel, then repeat and apply. You can also use Copy, click the destination, and choose Apply. Dollar signs keep references fixed, as in dollar A dollar one.

title: Open formula help
body:
Press F4, or click Help.

SUM       AVERAGE
MIN       MAX       COUNT

Return with Enter, Escape,
or the bottom button.
tip:
Function names are in English.
They work in formulas.
speech: Press F four, or click Help, to open the formula reference. It lists SUM, AVERAGE, MIN, MAX, and COUNT, with examples.
Function names are in English. Return to the sheet with Enter, Escape, or the button at the bottom.

title: Leave and return
body:
Exit / Escape returns
to the Spectrum menu.

Reopen Calculator to continue
in the same browser session.

Keep the page open
to retain your sheet.
code:
Save confirms a cell.
It does not save a file.
tip:
Reloading or closing the page
discards the sheet. This version
has no file save or CSV export.
speech: Click Exit, or press Escape outside an edit, to return to the Spectrum menu. Reopen Calculator to continue with your cells in the same browser session.
Keep the page open. Reloading or closing it discards the sheet. This version has no file save or C S V export; Save only confirms the current cell.
You are ready to build your own sheet.
